notes: One column of cards per agent under three set headings (map.js:2460): definitions the plugin ships, each card carrying model, tools and preloads; readers inside skills, grouped under the skill that spawns them; and the estate as name chips linking each repo's file. A segmented set control in the Skills tab's style and a search box narrow all three. Names peek the definition or skill file. The estate set needs a token and reads 0 headless.

The events are the list (map.js, the lifetimes section), each row a dot per layer coloured by the event's effect, so the list reads as the whole effect table; a pick redraws the detail beside it from a container width of 56rem and under it below that. The detail is the event's trigger and source links, one band per layer with its effect, evidence mark and lifetime ruler, and one card per copy of a skill. Below both, a worked week drawn as SVG lights the marks the picked event owns, and three lever cards close it. ?event= opens on an event; a pick does not write the address.

The Map's front door, where a bare ?view=map lands, as its Contents subview: every address under the tab that holds it, each a row of icon, name and its docs/map-tabs.csv sentence, and Contents' own row pinned in the primary colour with a map pin and "You are here", marked aria-current and opening nothing (map.js:1367). The rows are the TABS and SUBVIEWS arrays and the sentences the CSV's cells (overviewGroups, map.js:5843), so it keeps no list of its own. Groups flow in two balanced columns at lg (map.js:1040) and stack below it; each heading is full strength with its tab's icon and its rows indented under it, and on a phone the heading is held under the navigation. The search box narrows to rows whose name, tab, sentence or named files match, and then lists the matching files under the sentence (overviewFiles, map.js:5429). A row opens its address, which replaces Contents and is left by Back or the strip, hence swap-view; each row carries a data-at anchor, map-<key>. The subview strip switches to Purpose and Icons, the other readings under Overview.

Every family of icons in docs/icon-families.csv, under the three groups docs/vocabularies.csv names (Drawn marks, Phosphor glyphs, Emoji) (map.js:1398). Each family is a row of two columns at lg, stacked below it (map.js:1411): its label and member count, pending while the manifests load, and the passage that discusses its icons as a peek, seeded with that section or CSV row alone (loadIconDoc, map.js:6131); then its members as buttons of icon and name. Members are read from the source the row names, or by a reader in ICON_READERS (iconAll, map.js:6068), and drawn as the app draws them. Hover, focus or a tap opens one member's panel-tip (map.js:1477, showIconTip at map.js:6163): its name over its family with its Phosphor class (linking to the library) or its emoji's code points on one line; one link by the declaring file's short name, peeking the CSV row as written, the manifest entry or the code literal that declares it, or the SVG itself (iconTipSource, map.js:6221); the members sharing its glyph; and Find in code, which opens Search's Contents mode on the glyph, hence a jump out as well as the peek. The search box narrows members by name, repository, glyph or family. A two-way lens at the toolbar's right (map.js:1402) lists each glyph or emoji two or more members wear (iconShared, map.js:6096), each glyph opening the same tip. Each family carries a data-at anchor, icons-<family>.

Every group of peeves at once in balanced CSS columns (map.js, the peeves section): one row per peeve with a bar sized by sessions against the heaviest peeve, its id, short name and count, and icons marking a rule stated in a document or checked by a script. A two-way control groups by area or by where the rule is written. A row opens in place to the statement, what tripping it looks like, the owner document as peek links, and, with a token, the owner's quotes linking to their sessions; headless reads no quotes.

One object, docs/aims.json, drawn as four labeled sections: Mission, Goals, Initiatives and Reading (map.js:706). Each section is a 7rem label column beside its values at lg (map.js:707) and stacks above them below it. Copy as Markdown (map.js:698) renders the same object as text. Reading links open GitHub in a new tab (map.js:744) and the repo door navigates to the Repos view (map.js:751), so nothing in the body opens over or beside it.

One flat list over a strip of cards (linkedSwiper.attach, map.js:9451; markup map.js:2586): the groups of files sharing identical runs at the dial's threshold, marked =, then the pairs similar only in wording, marked ≈, each set under a sticky label (themeRows, map.js:9248). The range input in the toolbar (map.js:2568) decides which groups exist; the similar pairs keep a fixed cut. A card (themeCard, map.js:9300) numbers its files, then maps where each repeat sits in each file (themeLayout, map.js:9334; drawn by themeBars and themeDots, map.js:1263) under a switch of three views, Ribbons, Bars and Dot plot, that redraws every card at once (themeClick, map.js:9362). Below the map it shows each run in its file's own text with the run marked, then similar passages side by side from @2xl, less those overlapping a run (themeFill, map.js:9389); its file names open the in-app file deck (map.js:9416). The strip's door opens the cards as a deck (map.js:9462). The strip is sized to the Map pane's remaining height (themeFit, map.js:9426), so the pane does not scroll. Below 980px the list stacks over the strip.

Since 2026-10-20 one source table with the questions above it as a filter: a pick narrows the table and draws the question's relationship and declared paths between them, a second pick or Show all lists every source (map.js, the context section). A source name opens its panel-tip on hover, pinned by a click (ctxInspector, kits/panel-tip.js): each classified property drawn as its whole scale with the source's value lit, its connections and questions, and Read source opens the file deck. Question and pinned source are stamped as ctxtopic and ctxsource.

A line per table, grouped by repository and folder (map.js:3794), its columns as chips in their primitive's drawn mark and colour, grey where no registry declares one (map.js:3818). The primitive chips (map.js:3784) narrow the list to tables holding that primitive and fade every other column; the Registries chip (map.js:3761) switches to ?tab=registries, and the repository strip (map.js:3769) narrows by repository. A table's name or a chip opens one panel-tip (map.js:3842), pinned by a tap, whose ways out are kits/panel-tip.js's; its Open in Files leaves for the Files view (openDataFile, map.js:8211), a route change and not an overlay. Headless shows the public hub only, since the other repositories need a token.

map.js builds its own file deck on swipeDeck (openFileDeck, map.js:6146) rather than calling kits/file-deck.js; Distribution, Harness, Kits and Surfacing share it. The folder rail is map.js markup, shared with Harness. On a phone the reach chips wrap to three rows and the rail follows them, above the list. Job and answer (forms pass): opened with a documentation call, its edits are confirmed or discarded on the paragraphs and written as the call's answer line (lib/kits/call-answer.js:5).

The tab frames pages/doc-growth.html in an iframe (map.js:1267) rather than porting it, so the bubble chart, its Table switch and its play bar belong to that page, which loads daisyUI itself. The corpus strip (map.js:1236) picks the one payload the chart draws and appears only when more than one repository declares a growth path, read through a token (loadEstateGrowth, map.js:4934). Headless shows the hub corpus with no strip, so the selector and its select-show binding are coded from code. The figure's own row adds a min-edits range, coded dial, and switches for the measure (effort, net change, settled) and the unit (all words, prose only) that change how points are drawn rather than which exist; no frame code names those (pages/doc-growth.html, its controls row; added after this row's at).

A row of chips with counts leads since 2026-10-20 (automationToolbar), for what starts a file running: Event and Schedule open their own addresses, By hand, Called by code and No route filter the folder rail and the files under it, and the commit hook's row links to its steps on Events. The Docs arrangement again: invocation chips with counts that filter (map.js:3187), a folder rail with counts rolled up (map.js:3207), and the selected folder's direct files (map.js:3249). A title or the deck door opens the folder's files in the shared openFileDeck (openHarnessDeck, map.js:6992). The rail goes beside the files at the viewport lg breakpoint (map.js:3202), while Docs switches on its container (map.js:1414) for the docked deck reason given at map.js:1303, so one arrangement answers a docked deck two ways. On a phone the chips wrap to four rows and the rail sits above the files, more than a screen down. A standing sentence explains the badges (map.js:3170).

One section per kind of event, in the order a change meets them: the environment build, the Claude Code session, git, then GitHub Actions, each under a sticky heading with its count (map.js, the events section). Claude Code's section is every event it accepts a hook on (docs/hook-events.csv) in columns by phase, four at 2xl, two from md, one on a phone, with an event dimmed when nothing is registered. An event row is its name and meaning, then what runs on it: the plugin's registrations with their matcher, the session-*.sh files the dispatcher runs, and the commit hook's steps listed open under pre-commit. A script name opens every file on the view as a file deck. Opened from Automation's trigger row.

One list flowed into two columns from xl (map.js:3331), filtered by the boot, demo and untested chips (map.js:3311). A name or the deck door opens the filtered list in openFileDeck (openKitDeck, map.js:7113). The demo badge navigates to the demo as an app view (kitDemoHref, map.js:7107), a route change. A standing sentence under the chip explains the rows (map.js:3301), beside the lede that already does. Namespace, load and line counts carry title-tips.

One card per row of docs/outposts.csv, two columns from xl (map.js:3387), each a definition list of the outpost's parts (map.js:3405), so the card is written for the type. Addresses in the list are x-blob links that peek their source. The account-skills card spans both columns and adds the last recorded observation, which needs a token and shows a sign-in line headless (map.js:3422).

A topic rail beside one column of rule cards (map.js:1633), narrowed by a search (map.js:1596), Level and Origin chips with counts (map.js:1603), and the rail. It is the Docs and Harness arrangement built a third way: btn-xs neutral chips where they use bordered pills, a solid primary pick in the rail (map.js:1651) where they tint, and below lg a Topic toggle that hides the rail (map.js:1636) where theirs stacks above the list. A routes diagram: the hub, one edge per use value in docs/portable.csv labeled with its count, the set of estate repositories, and the outposts joined to the repository each declares. Laid out as a grid with an SVG layer drawing curves between the placed boxes (reachMeasure), so at phone width the grid stacks and the outpost lines drop, each outpost naming its repository in its own box. Every node opens a panel-tip in place (hover where the pointer is fine, a click or tap pins it), each in a form of its own: a repository as the Repos card (its one-line note, the alignment verdict and checks as chips, a row of icon counts), a route as its files in name chips grouped by kind, an outpost as its mechanism (declared and observed side by side, the check, the record). A chip opens the swipe deck over that route's files, under which the pinned panel waits; the ways out to Distribution, Outposts or GitHub sit in the panel's header. Node borders carry GitHub visibility; without a token only the hub and the repositories an outpost names are drawn.

The Tables list (map.js:3754) narrowed to the hub's registries and grouped by key primitive, locator keys then id keys (tableGroups, map.js:8385). A registry's panel-tip (map.js:3873) holds what its card held: gloss, key and identity, target, scope, property totals, gate and renders-in files, each file peeking through x-blob. The Registries chip (map.js:3761) is on, and the repository strip is not drawn.

Rows grouped by delivery route, the groups side by side in two or three columns by container width (map.js:807) and stacked one above another on a phone. A title opens the visible rows as one deck at that row (openItem, map.js:4168). A folder row opens the Files view instead, and the owner door switches to the Skills, Docs or Automation tab with its filter set (openSetOwner, map.js:4136). The comment at map.js:6112 records that this tab once navigated to Files and moved to the deck so the reader keeps the set.

Since 2026-10-27 one list over a strip of cards (map.js, the showing section), on the linked-swiper kit as Peeves is: groups for Links, Grammar, Modes, Routes, Paste and Kinds, a row per record on one line, a link row carrying its three marks under the Links heading's icons. One column of cards per skill under set headings (map.js:2148, map.js:2177), narrowed by search and two census lines: the set control drawn in the segmented tab style (map.js:2093) and the subject badges (map.js:2117), kept apart on purpose per the comment at map.js:2084. The set gloss under the control is standing prose that changes with the pick (map.js:2103). Names peek SKILL.md. The estate set needs a token and reads 0 headless (map.js:2210).

One card per primitive in two columns (map.js:918). A card title docks the deck where the window allows, lands on the bullet the card paraphrases, and scrolls the card back into view (openSurfAt, map.js:4650). Below the 1024px dock width the same deck opens over the cards, which is the phone change. The deck door (map.js:888) and the region doors (showRegion, map.js:4685) open it undocked. Drawn inside Automation since 2026-10-20, opened from its trigger row, whose chips carry counts (automationToolbar). One card per task in web-tools-private's scheduled-tasks.csv, grouped under a heading per runner (map.js, the scheduled section). A card carries the task id, status and authority badges with title tips, the entry file as a GitHub link, the schedule read from its cron into words with the next firing in local time, the events that also start its workflow and the inputs the scheduled-tasks workflow passes (read from the workflow file), what it keeps, and its last run (the state file, or the Actions API for a dispatched workflow); a workflow still carrying its own cron is flagged. A task run inside the scheduled-tasks workflow adds its stage ladder, four across at xl and one column on a phone. The registry chips open in a peek. With a token, a pencil on a GitHub-hosted card opens an editor in place under the schedule: status, then hourly, daily, weekly, monthly or a raw cron, in local time, with the cron it would write and its next firing; Save commits one row of the registry. Needs a token, and shows one line saying so headless.

A diagram of docs/writers.csv in three columns laid out by a grid, with an SVG layer drawing curves between the placed boxes (writersMeasure), as the Routes diagram does: what starts a writer (you, an event, time); the writers, boxed by the machine they run on, an agent carrying its model badge and a person drawn as one; and where they set (a local copy, a working branch, main). A dotted loop joins a writer to a writer it starts, dashed where that writer polls. Hovering or tapping any box lights the lines and boxes it connects to. A picked writer opens a card under the diagram with the same relations in words, how it sets (replace, append, propose, merge), its definition as a GitHub link, how its commits read in the Writes view, flagged where a non-person's read as a person's own, and the docs/direct-to-main.csv processes it sets on main directly. Labels and glosses come from docs/vocabularies.csv. At phone width the columns stack and the lines drop; the card carries them. Public data, so it renders without a token.

Three labeled chip rows, each a dimension with file and assertion counts, filter the suite (map.js:2671); rows group by method in two columns at lg (map.js:2715). A title or the deck door opens what the filters left in openFileDeck (openTestDeck, map.js:6898). Two registry-wide toggles, names and compared, expand every row at once (map.js:2631). In the estate needs a token and shows a sign-in line headless (map.js:2834). On a phone the chip rows wrap to six lines above the list.

Rows of app routes ranked by last code change and folded under their nav stop (map.js:3557), with a census line of counts that does not filter (map.js:3514). A caret expands a row in place to its files and open pull requests (map.js:3631, map.js:3642); an openable label navigates to that view (openAppView, map.js:4350), a route change. Ranking and dating come from kits/route-activity.js and kits/route-join.js (map.js:4243, map.js:4331). The pane is a full-bleed iframe of pages/toss-render.html (app/index.html:1297), so the body is whatever page the address names. Shot as ?app=mehrlander/web-tools:pages/text-lab.html, which drew its own tabs, status chips and probe list; that arrangement belongs to the guest's row. The address goes into the frame and nothing comes back out (app/index.html:7543), so navigation inside the frame is not stamped and the binding is none. App views default to nav mode (app/index.html:2175): the header gains the page's own lit button and the sidebar starts closed at every width, so the phone shot differs only in width. The view is an iframe of pages/repo-atlas.html (app/index.html:1795), pinned to the default branch (app/index.html:5519). A zoomable canvas treemap is the main region (repo-atlas.html:142). Repo and ref boxes pick the one repo drawn, and a file filter narrows the tiles (repo-atlas.html:80, 92). The right rail holds This view, File types and Largest files (repo-atlas.html:147); a type row isolates one category on the map (repo-atlas.html:154), so the rail filters. A tile click selects a file into the rail's selection panel (repo-atlas.html:792), the select-show tie coded; filter also holds. A directory click zooms the map in place and the crumbs walk back up (repo-atlas.html:121), which no reach code holds. Phone: the page has no breakpoint. The rail keeps w-72 and the map is squeezed to a strip about 75px wide, while the header's filter box runs off screen. A tap opens the visible list as a deck at that row, each slide mounting the branchBrief component (estate.js:11490); &detail= is stamped. The deck covers the view pane at lg and the window below it. A deep link to a branch the filter hides opens a deck of one. The scope chips are BRANCH_SCOPES (estate.js:8624); whether they carry counts was not checked. The Activity tab row and search box every Activity pane shares were added after the Activity reader found them missing. A frontier banner per provider sits above the list (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3288) and ends in a sentence of explanatory prose. Provider chips and a Hand chip carry counts and filter the loaded months (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3350); a Search the archive button hands the query to the Search view's Chats lane (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3344). One row per chat (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3386) with the same left-rail card class the Sessions and Branches rows use (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:1972, 3208, 3387), copied rather than shared. Paged one month per tap (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3429). Not shot with data: the chats-pane scenario reads a chat-histories checkout this sandbox lacks, so coded from code.

The open repo's .web-tools.json as a form beside its raw JSON (config.js:125). Both panes edit one object: a form edit re-serializes the draft and a JSON edit re-parses into the form (config.js:9), so the tie is two-way. Coded tool rather than fields because every labeled value is an input and the pane exists to save, with a Save bar stuck to its foot (config.js:465). The form sections are General, Projects, Pages and Stage, laid out by container queries (config.js:139). The Field reference is a closed details block over docs/manifest-fields.csv that opens in place with its own key filter (config.js:411). Below lg a Settings and JSON pill shows one pane at a time (config.js:110), confirmed by the phone shot. The folder tree (pathPicker inline, file-browser.js:52) sits over a strip of the folder's files, one shared viewer per slide (file-browser.js:221). Coded linked-swiper, not header-swiper, because the top region is an index into the strip and the selection runs both ways. A tree pick sets sel and place() scrolls the strip to it (file-browser.js:108, 160). A swipe sets at, which writes sel back and marks and scrolls the tree's row (file-browser.js:109, 204, 212). The header comment calls this the branch detail's shape (file-browser.js:3), which the pilot coded header-swiper; the geometry is borrowed and the binding is not. The strip is a hand snap track with its own go(), stripScroll() and lazy mount (file-browser.js:85, 141 to 199), the job swipeDeck.core does with track, go, active and onSlide. The deck door beside it already uses the kit's open and drill (file-browser.js:284), and that deck moves this view's position on each slide (file-browser.js:275). Descending a folder re-scopes the strip, so the crumbs act as a selector over folders; left uncoded because the tree is the list half of the body. The record deck is the viewer's, reached on a tabular file (viewer.js:2893); with path=docs the strip opened on account-skills.csv as a Tabulator grid. Top over bottom at both widths; below sm only the pager arrows drop (file-browser.js:70).

The repo's README rendered as prose (app/index.html:1469) under a head of the repo's own facts: name, description, visibility, stars, forks, default branch and push age as badges, and an Atlas button (app/index.html:1446). Defined inline as overview() (app/index.html:8287); the markdown goes through mdDoc.html when the kit is loaded and marked otherwise (app/index.html:2052). Nothing opens over the body: the Atlas button and the README's links navigate away. The head is a layout written for a repo, hence form repo. Pin over To-do over Jot over Ping over Note in one pane (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3574), each section its own heading, capture form and inner scroll: Pin capped at 35% of the height (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3594) and the other four sharing the rest as flex-1 shares (lib/alpineComponents/estate.js:3756, 4064, 4218, 4293). One card per page, three columns at lg (app/index.html:1373). Each card has a thumbnail face that toggles in place among screenshot, live iframe and HTML source (app/index.html:1396), a title, and doors to the Files view and GitHub. The workspace README, rendered through mdHtml, which calls mdDoc.html (app/index.html:1636, app/index.html:2126); a first heading that repeats the project's name is dropped, since the masthead already says it (app/index.html:4940). A mode of the Files tab, chosen in the All files and Docs switch under the tab row (app/index.html:1586) and addressed as &tab=docs. Every markdown file under the workspace, from one recursive tree read, as a folder tree with counts rolled up: the first level open, deeper folders waiting for a tap, READMEs leading their folder (projectDocsRows, app/index.html:4851; rows at app/index.html:1776).
